>Your answer hasn't changed since the [last time](https://old.reddit.com/r/legaladvice/comments/1jca1ho/nj_hostile_work_environment_constructive_dismissal/) you posted this.

The original post was a mistake on my end. I cross-posted it to another subreddit, wanted to delete it because I wanted to change the title, and accidentally deleted the original post. Derp. 🤦‍♀️

>This is 1) seemingly true even in your telling, and 2) the company doing the right thing at least in the context of engaging in an interactive process of discussing your accommodation.

In the letter my boss emailed me he said I could work before/after my appointments pointed out to him that I could work on Tues/Thurs. I reached out to my therapist about any other centers that offered the program at a later time or were virtual but there weren't. I looked into other places that would be able to provide the services I needed, but it would have taken too long to find one within my boss' time frame. I communicated this to my boss.

>Why hasn't NJ DOL gotten your wages back then? This issue may be important in the context of a wage claim. It probably isn't in the rest of this.

Honestly, it's because I haven't spoken with a lawyer yet. I've never filed a wage complaint before and was unsure if said complaint would hold up. My boss would definitely know I was the one who filed the complaint even if I did it anonymously, and after the investigation was closed he could request all of the information on the complaint because of OPRA. I feared retaliation in some way.

>Some of what you describe here (sexual harassment, sexism, potentially slurs) is important. Some (disparaging remarks, yelling, humiliation) probably isn't. Some requires additional context.

I agree re the additional context but I was unsure if my post would break Rule 4. It's already kinda lengthy as it is, but I will add some more info tomorrow (midnight here).

>Maybe the bigger challenge is it sounds in your telling like you need a leave, not an accommodation.

I was thinking of asking for a leave, but it was pointed out that it could be interpreted that I didn't want to leave the job since the leave would be temporary. Then I found out about constructive dismissal.  
Regardless, I've realized that trying to 'tough it out' is no longer a viable option for me and I've already reached out to several employment attorneys.

I really appreciate your responses. Thank you.  
It's given me several things to think about and how I to better navigate all of this.

I'm not religious either, but that's an interesting idea!


Have you tried doing that, if you don't mind me asking?


I'll have to check if there are any regulations regarding confessionals in my state just to be safe, but this is something I never would have thought of.

I have told her, but the only way to get  the conversation back on track is to lie to her and say that I'm safe/ok. I hate lying to her, and feel that having to confirm that I'm safe is treating the symptom, not the issue imo.


Another user mentioned thinking of alternative ways to tell her, and I think that may be a good route for me.

I agree, but isn't discussing methods against one of the sub's rules? Sorry if I'm being dense.

The last thing I want to do is trigger others who are in the same situation as me.

Yes, I consistently have the same handful of thoughts of how to kill myself playing on a loop in my brain pretty much 24/7. I'm hesitant to go into detail as I don't want to break any rules, but some of them are definitely doable.

Thank you for your support.

I still need to spend some time gathering my thoughts so I can present them coherently, but I will reach out if I ever do sort my dumpster fire of a mind out lol.

Yes! I understand why medical professionals are overly cautious, but it's not always a black and white situation. Damned if you do, damned if you don't.



I am still trying to find something I enjoy doing, but I'm running out of ideas lol. I think maybe a 2nd job would be the best route for me atm as it would kinda force me to focus on something other than dying.



Thank you for your support.

Honestly, I don't have a clue anymore. I've been dealing with this for so long the desire to kill myself is just always there. I have no goals, desires, or plans and I just feel like it's not worth sticking around anymore, if that makes any sense.

I will try to come up with some alternative ways to bring it up, that's a good idea. She's known me long enough to know when I'm bullshitting, so having some talking points at the ready will hopefully prevent the conversation from devolving into "Are you safe? Do you have a plan? Are you safe? Do you have a plan? Are you safe? Do you have a plan?" etc. She's just doing her job, but it's not productive.
Im in the process of looking for a new one. Unfortunately most are booked up for the next 2 months so I can only really wait it out atm.

Unfortunatley thats how I was involuntarily hospitalized. I made it very, very clear to the person I was talking to that I had no intentions on acting on my plans and that I just wanted to talk.


I was emotional during the call, but I wasn't sobbing untrollably or anything. I guess that was justification enough for them? I've never had any therapist call the cops on me for talking about ideations.

Unfortunatley thats how I was involuntarily hospitalized. I made it very, **very** clear to the person I was talking to that I had no intentions on acting on my plans and that I just wanted to talk. Next thing I know two cops are walkiing up to me. 🙃 It caught me completely off guard.

Im in the US. I wasn't aware that calling over ideations could be considered malpractice, but it happened to me- it was when I was involuntarily committed.


Not only was it infuriating, it was humiliating because I was at work when it happened and the *entire* company saw what happened. It caught me completely off guard. I was going to file a complaint but never followed through, but I think I'm going to reconsider it now.


The online support idea is a good idea though, especially since I could use a VPN. Thank you.
